races.name: Newly Weds Sara & Nigel Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Griffin Auctioneers Maiden

runners_data.name: Davy Crockett
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained with a credible class profile and Good-ground form, but this is a horse whose natural instinct is to be ridden from well off the pace — squeezed to midfield on the map because the field is saturated with hold-up types, which means he is unlikely to secure the deep position he needs to produce his best.|

runners_data.name: Nothingbutadream
runners_data.note: Finished 10th and 15th in recent starts with a noted tendency to fade in the finish; Chris Timmons has 0 wins from 2 runners in the last 14 days, and the 99-day absence adds further uncertainty — very hard to be bullish.|

runners_data.name: Onlytheriverknows
runners_data.note: Debutant with no public form line and an unknown going profile — Darragh O'Keeffe provides experienced guidance but there is simply no evidence base on which to assess this runner's chance.|

runners_data.name: Solness
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, trained by Joseph O'Brien (strong 14-day strike rate of 7/56) and ridden by the high-class J J Slevin; has positional form on Good ground and controls the pace map entirely — the key question is whether he has enough left in the tank over 1m4f having been off 16 days.|

runners_data.name: Glittering Gem
runners_data.note: D K Weld filly stepping up significantly in trip from a career best of 10f, but she showed genuine ability placing twice on Good ground and her prominent style suits a race where the leader can be tracked comfortably; the trip is the one unknown.|

runners_data.name: Kaleo Ametsa
runners_data.note: Six-year-old gelding that Josh Halley has campaigned consistently without reward — zero wins from nine runs, all on Good, and here he is shown in midfield rather than his preferred deep hold-up berth because the rear of the field is too crowded with similar types.|

runners_data.name: Keep It Together
runners_data.note: Has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, sits eight days since its last run, and the form figures of 6-12-14 on comparable going speak plainly — the trip and profile offer little encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Shirzan
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Soft for P G Fahey and placed twice on similar ground; returning after 97 days and switching to Good for the first time since a 6th on Good over 18f — the trip suits, but the fitness query and jockey claim (O'Gorman, 7lb) need factoring in.|

runners_data.name: Aiteall
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien three-year-old whose sole run produced a 13th over a much shorter 9f trip on Good — not only is this a huge step up in distance, but this runner is a true hold-up type shown in midfield due to the congested rear, carrying a fade-in-finish warning and the lowest weight on style-fit confidence.|

runners_data.name: Metallic
runners_data.note: Another O'Brien debutant with no public form whatsoever; Julian Pietropaolo rides with a 7lb claim but there is no going, trip or style evidence to assess — an entirely unknown quantity.|

races.paceDynamic: Solness is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-horse maiden and, with no genuine pace rival willing or able to press him, J J Slevin can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the 1m4f trip on Good turf at Tramore. The absence of early pressure means the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the pack behind and reduces the advantage of a late run from deep. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent types who can travel economically in mid-division and produce a sustained finish — but crucially, this field holds more true hold-up horses than can all be placed naturally at the rear, with Davy Crockett, Kaleo Ametsa, and Aiteall redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all settle in their preferred position. Front-running and prominent profiles benefit most here: Solness controls the race and any horse travelling smoothly just off the pace, able to quicken on Good ground in the straight, is best placed to exploit the modest, uncontested tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solness Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Solness is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the pace stays moderate enough that his rivals never fully wind up their challenge.
scenarios.body: Slevin dictates every yard at a comfortable clip, saving enough for the straight, and the tidy gallop means no rival gets a decisive finishing kick from the rear; the shape suits Solness and anything travelling prominently just behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just sufficient to stretch the field and a horse sitting second or third rouses in the straight to reel in Solness.
scenarios.body: A horse like Glittering Gem or Shirzan, tracking the leader without over-exerting, hits the front inside the final furlong as Solness's stamina is tested over 1m4f; Good ground and a modest tempo reward the energy-efficient prominent mover.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the field bunches, allowing a midfield runner to find a gap and finish strongly through tired rivals.
scenarios.body: A horse like Davy Crockett, even racing out of his deepest hold-up role, can use his class edge (trained by Mullins, recent 1m1f win on Good) to pick his way through a compacted field in the straight; the redistribution tempers confidence but a slow overall time narrows the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens mid-race, stringing the field out and leaving a genuine back-marker with a clear run to finish fastest.
scenarios.body: This requires the race to be run at a genuinely strong tempo — unlikely given only one pace-setter — but if it materialises, Shirzan (won on Soft, unexposed at the trip) could be the beneficiary; Kaleo Ametsa and Aiteall, both racing out of their natural rear positions, are style-fit discounts here.

watchPoints.text: Solness (Slevin/O'Brien) is the sole pace-setter — if he gets a completely uncontested lead at a dawdling gallop, the race could be over sooner than rivals anticipate and any horse slow to respond turning for home will have no chance of bridging the gap.

Glittering Gem is making a significant step up from 10f to 1m4f for D K Weld — if she fails to see out the trip on this prominent-running style, she could weaken sharply in the final two furlongs and compromise those directly behind her.

Davy Crockett and Kaleo Ametsa are both true hold-up horses forced into midfield positions — watch the early stages to see whether either rider attempts to drop back to their natural ground, which could cause crowding and interference as the field settles.

Three O'Brien runners (Solness, Aiteall, Metallic) in a 10-horse field raises the possibility of team tactics — Aiteall or Metallic could be used to serve Solness's lead rather than running their own race, which would make the pace even more controlled.|

Both Onlytheriverknows and Metallic are debutants — in a low-grade maiden on Good turf, an unexposed runner with a well-regarded trainer can show unexpected early pace or drop away tamely; watch the opening exchanges for any surprise moves from either.|

races.name: Morris DIY Rated Race

runners_data.name: Maxminelli
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trained by De Bromhead who has solid each-way form at 10f-12f on Good ground (0W3P in similar going); Darragh O'Keeffe booked, stepping up in trip to 1m4f which his pedigree and style should suit, and this is his most race-fit recent spell.|

runners_data.name: Sunrush
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has not won in four recent starts and whose Good-ground form (2 runs, no wins, no places) is modest; 72 days off and a 5lb claimer in the saddle are concerns, but as one of only two pacemakers he will likely dictate early sectionals whether he wants to or not.|

runners_data.name: Rodeo Blues
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground at 10f-11f give him the most compelling recent form in the field; hold-up style suits a race where the two leaders battle each other, and the 7lb claimer Pietropaolo is a significant weight advantage, though the 16-day turnaround after two quick wins is worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Tanzanite Diamond
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with placed form at 10f-12f on Good ground wearing a tongue strap; gelded and lightly framed at 140lbs, nine days since last run suggests connections are happy, but six runs without a win and a last-time-out zero are difficult to overcome in a competitive 1m4f handicap.|

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose natural rear position is compressed in this pace-heavy field; stepping up markedly from 8f where all five recent runs have been is an untested trip, and the Noel Meade yard have had only 1 winner from 23 runners in 14 days — her redistributed map position understates how far back she will actually race.|

runners_data.name: A Pretty Penny
runners_data.note: Has a win at 10f on Good ground and placed form at 12f, so the trip genuinely suits; the 7lb claim from Shay Wallace is useful, but as a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping in this pace-rich field, she is unlikely to secure any kind of prominent berth and her chance depends on a true end-to-end gallop.|

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, 10 days since last run and four runs without a place finish; Good-ground form is moderate and she is the shorter-priced of the two pacemakers to crack under pressure, but her presence is tactically important because she ensures Sunrush faces genuine early competition.|

runners_data.name: Tickle The Cat
runners_data.note: The pace data flags a tendency to fade in the finish, which is a significant flag for a horse already tagged as a true hold-up type who will be racing well off the speed in a contested-pace race; three runs only (0W0P), all on Ground that ranges from Good to Heavy, and the 52-day break adds uncertainty over current fitness.|

races.paceDynamic: Sunrush and Mare Crisium are both confirmed front-runners in a field of eight over 1m4f at Tramore on Good ground, meaning the lead will be contested from the off and neither will get a free gallop. The resulting honest, pressured pace across the race's early and middle stages is likely to stretch the field and drain reserves, setting up conditions that reward gallopers who travel well through the race rather than those who need a late sprint to materialise. Rodeo Blues, who has back-to-back wins on Good ground at 10f-11f and is the form pick from the hold-up group, is well-placed in theory, though the redistribution of Love Orchid, A Pretty Penny, and Tickle The Cat — all genuine hold-up horses pushed forward on the map because the field is rear-heavy — means true closers will be bunched and may struggle to find clear daylight late. The race shape firmly favours a prominent racer or a hold-up horse with a strong enough cruising speed to travel in the slipstream of the front two and pick them off in the final two furlongs; Maxminelli, racing prominently with De Bromhead's shrewd handling of 3yo handicappers, fits that profile most naturally in this setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sunrush and Mare Crisium battle for the lead and burn each other out by halfway, the horse sitting second or third throughout collects.
scenarios.body: The two leaders set an honest, pressured gallop that compromises their own finishing efforts, leaving the prominent racer closest in behind with first run turning in; this distance and going suits a horse that can travel fluently and sustain its effort to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to create a strong tempo that stretches the race and opens ground in the straight for a deep closer.
scenarios.body: Rodeo Blues has two recent wins on Good ground at 10f-11f and is the most credible finisher in the field; the 7lb claimer Julian Pietropaolo takes off enough weight to make the hold-up style viable if the pace truly collapses the front runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Sunrush or Mare Crisium secures an uncontested lead after the other fades or misses the break, allowing a solo rail gallop at a controlled pace.
scenarios.body: A horse that dictates terms on Good ground over 1m4f at Tramore can set a sustainable rhythm and simply outstay rivals who never get into a rhythm tracking them; Sunrush's recent experience and positive draw makes this the more likely candidate of the two to survive the early duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Shock Result
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final bend and multiple horses come wide in the straight without a winner emerging cleanly.
scenarios.body: In a messy finish on Good ground the redistributed hold-up horses shuffled back by the field's pace bias may find gaps late, with A Pretty Penny's Good-ground win at 10f giving her some credibility if the race shape scrambles; Tanzanite Diamond's placed form at this trip could also bring her into play.

watchPoints.text: Watch the early duel between Sunrush and Mare Crisium — if both push aggressively for the lead in the first furlong the pace could become unsustainably fast, dramatically increasing the chance of a hold-up horse finishing strongly down the outside.

Rodero Blues carries a back-to-back winner's penalty in confidence but his claimer Pietropaolo is unproven over this course and trip — watch how quickly he moves into contention on the final bend, as a wide move too early could cost him the race.

Love Orchid, A Pretty Penny, and Tickle The Cat are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into the midfield on the map — if all three end up jostling for the same late ground in the straight, traffic and interference become a real risk in the closing stages.

Maxminelli races with hood (hg:t) which can sharpen a horse's early focus; watch whether O'Keeffe uses that to slot him into a clean second or third position behind the two leaders rather than being carried wide by the congested midfield group.

Tramore's 1m4f course tends to favour horses who travel kindly through the race rather than those who require a strong late injection — if the going softens marginally during the card (already confirmed Good throughout) watch for any horse that has a higher TS rating relative to its RPR, as class of speed may matter over raw stamina.

races.name: Strand Inn Dunmore East Handicap

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Adrian McGuinness with J J Slevin up; sole win came on Soft in 12f which raises stamina questions at this trip on Good, and similar-going form reads a poor 7 runs without a win or place, making her hard to fancy from the back.|

runners_data.name: Stepdance
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's mare has strong recent form (three wins in last five on Good ground) and takes the lead comfortably here, but STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects she is lightly matched as an outright front-runner for this yard — her dominant position is genuine, yet rivals will be watching every move she makes.|

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan runner wearing hood (tp) who finished 3rd over 12f on Good last time; naturally a hold-up type but Daniel King may look to secure a handy midfield pitch given the traffic concerns further back, and the extra two furlongs of this trip looks within range.|

runners_data.name: Mullacurry Maid
runners_data.note: Donal Kinsella filly fitted with tongue-tie who fades in finish and has a patchy record at 37 days between runs; naturally races from the rear but the surplus of hold-up horses in this field means she's unlikely to get clear air and those late-fade tendencies are a further concern.|

runners_data.name: Preparations
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's five-year-old has shown glimpses over this sort of trip (4th over 10f on Soft) but is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map; Sam Coen's 5lb claim is useful, though 26 days off and uninspiring recent form (0, 6 in last two) temper expectations.|

runners_data.name: Metamorpheus
runners_data.note: Consistent stayer who has placed in five of his last five starts over 12f-18f on Good, Andrew McNamara's seven-year-old is the standout hold-up profile in this field with proven finishing power at this distance and going combination — the redistribution to midfield on the map understates how far back he'll likely sit.|

runners_data.name: Go Flo Jo
runners_data.note: Jessica O'Gorman (7) partners this P G Fahey filly returning after a massive 267-day break; a confirmed hold-up type with a tendency to fade in the finish, and the combination of a long absence and amateur rider makes this a very speculative runner from the back of the field.|

runners_data.name: Spinning Web
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns (5) takes the ride for Margaret Mullins on this blinkered six-year-old who is a natural prominent racer; solid sim-going record (2W 4P in 15) and 69 days off is not a concern for a horse capable of tracking Stepdance from just off the lead in an uncontested shape.|

runners_data.name: Limestone Red
runners_data.note: Tracey Collins runner wearing a hood (p) who recorded a win over 10f on Soft; a natural hold-up type shifted into midfield because of field congestion, and a 31-day absence combined with poor Tramore-trip form (0W 1P in 15 on Good) limits confidence.|

runners_data.name: Nathema
runners_data.note: Jimmy Dalton (7) aboard Andrew Slattery's three-year-old fitted with a hood (p); consistent placed efforts but yet to win in four runs, all of which have ended in finishes of 8th or 4th — the fade tendency and amateur booking do not help in a race this competitive.|

runners_data.name: Duleek Street
runners_data.note: John C McConnell's eight-year-old returns after a staggering 377-day absence fitted with a tongue-tie and is a natural hold-up type who has been off the track for over a year; six-placing form (0W 2P in 15 on Good) and extreme layoff make this a very difficult profile to support.|

races.paceDynamic: Stepdance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge her lead, she is set to dictate from the front at a tempo entirely of her own choosing on Good ground at Tramore. Spinning Web is the only other prominent-style runner and is likely to slot in behind Stepdance, meaning the early sectionals will be controlled and unhurried rather than pressured or contested. The remainder of the field — including Preparations, Mullacurry Maid, Metamorpheus, Go Flo Jo, Limestone Red and Duleek Street — are natural hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because the field contains far more hold-up horses than the pace shape can naturally accommodate at the rear; of those, Metamorpheus, Preparations and Tassarolo are most likely to actually press forward and secure a realistic midfield pitch. A single front-runner dictating a measured pace on a flat Good-ground course over 1m4f strongly favours the horses immediately tracking the leader in the prominent-to-midfield berths, as those runners will be on the bridle throughout and ideally placed to pounce in the straight without having to make up ground from the back of the pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stepdance Controls, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Stepdance sets a sustainable lead and no rival applies serious pressure, turning the race into a test of positional efficiency.
scenarios.body: Stepdance bowls along at a comfortable gallop, and the two or three horses sitting closest to her — Spinning Web and any prominent-tracking midfielders — conserve energy before producing their challenge from the home turn; the race becomes a sprint for those best placed turning in rather than a stamina test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Finishers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Stepdance goes too fast early and ties up in the straight, allowing hold-up horses with reserves to mow her down.
scenarios.body: Without a stablemate to regulate, Stepdance burns energy making all and runs out of petrol in the final two furlongs, handing an advantage to any horse with genuine staying power who has been conserving energy from further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Class Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a flat, even tempo and becomes a test of raw ability in the straight rather than tactical positioning.
scenarios.body: A uniform gallop compresses the field and removes positional advantage, meaning horses with the best form figures and recent peak ratings rise to the top in a straight-line gallop home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Hold-Up Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant traffic trouble or a pace collapse that opens up late ground for genuine deep hold-up types.
scenarios.body: The crowded midfield of redistributed horses creates interference turning for home, and a horse that threads through late — one with genuine sustained finishing pace — arrives from the back to catch tired rivals.

watchPoints.text: Stepdance — watch whether she gets an uncontested lead at a crawl; if she dictates every fraction unchallenged, she becomes very difficult to dislodge and the race may be over turning for home.

Spinning Web — if she tracks Stepdance closely from the jump and the pace remains manageable, she is perfectly positioned to mount a challenge but her 69-day absence needs to have left her fit enough to sustain it.

Metamorpheus — given the congestion of hold-up types throughout the field, watch for potential traffic trouble on the home turn as numerous riders seek a clear run simultaneously; his finishing kick could be wasted if he meets a wall of horses.

Go Flo Jo — a 267-day layoff warrants monitoring in the paddock and at the start; if she shows any signs of greenness or reluctance, her already slim chance from the back of the pack is effectively gone.

Mullacurry Maid — her pattern of fading late combined with 37 days off and a field shape that will deny her a clean hold-up run makes her worth tracking as a market mover rather than a likely winner; unusual support would be informative.

races.name: Perennial Freight Handicap

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won over 12f and 13f on good ground and arrives fresh on just 3 days' rest; maps here as the lone pace-setter and gets a dream opportunity to dictate, though the [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects that this prominent-labelled horse must perform in an actual lead role, which is a slightly different ask.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse trained by K J Condon, who has a 1/6 14-day strike rate, and she arrives in good order on 6 days' rest; her win at 10f on good ground is encouraging, and with the pace likely slow she will need to take closer order than usual to be competitive over this trip.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 10f and 12f on good ground and is the hold-up runner with the most convincing recent form for this trip; apprentice Reese Holohan takes 7lbs off but placing a natural closer in a slowly-run race off one front-runner increases tactical difficulty.

runners_data.name: Expound
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer equipped with a tongue-strap and returning from 93 days off, which is a significant fitness question mark; if sharp enough, his natural proximity to the pace gives him a tactical edge in a race that is unlikely to be run at a searching gallop.

runners_data.name: Churchwarden
runners_data.note: Trained by Henry De Bromhead, who has strong stable form (4/35 over 14 days), and finished 2nd over 16f on good ground — a profile that fits the trip; however, his true running style is hold-up and he is pushed into a midfield slot by the volume of closers in this field, meaning he may not get the strong pace he needs.

runners_data.name: Rakki
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained and has placed over 16f on good ground, giving him a legitimate trip profile; a genuine hold-up operator who has been mapped to midfield only because of overcrowding at the rear, and a slowly-run Tramore race off one front-runner is an awkward scenario for his true style.

runners_data.name: Berto Ramirez
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on good ground and has placed at 12f, so trip stamina is real; naturally a hold-up horse nudged forward on the map by the surplus of closers in this field, and with trainer Andrew McNamara showing 0/10 in the 14-day window, there is limited confidence from the yard angle.

races.paceDynamic: Daboya is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Expound as a potential prominent challenger, will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m4f trip on good ground at Tramore. With no genuine pace rivals to press Daboya, the tempo is likely to be measured and tactical, rewarding a horse that can sit close enough to the pace to strike when the sprint begins rather than needing a strong gallop to get competitive. Marmeladova, Merlin The Wizard, Churchwarden, Rakki, and Berto Ramirez are all natural hold-up horses, but the map cannot accommodate that many closers at the rear — Churchwarden, Rakki, and Berto Ramirez are redistributed to midfield because the field simply has too many hold-up types to allow all of them to operate from their preferred position. In a slowly-run race off a single front-runner, the race shape strongly favours horses that are positioned prominently or just off the pace, as a slow-tempo miler-and-a-half on good ground is unlikely to generate the strong late pace that pure closers need to get competitive from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Daboya Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya leads at a comfortable clip and no rival applies sustained pressure, turning the race into a controlled procession.
scenarios.body: Daboya settles in front at a pace of his own choosing, and the prominent runners behind him track comfortably without burning energy; the lack of a genuine challenge means the winner likely comes from the first two or three in the running order.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya's lead is covered entering the straight and a close-tracking rival swoops at the turn for home.
scenarios.body: Expound or Marmeladova, travelling just off the pace, is best positioned to pounce as soon as Daboya is headed; at a true mile-and-a-half on good ground, fitness and class from a handy position will decide it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and creates enough of a gap in the straight for a late finisher to thread through.
scenarios.body: Merlin The Wizard, who has won at 1m2f on good ground and is proven over the trip, is the hold-up type with the most convincing form profile to make up ground; Churchwarden, though redistributed to midfield, retains the class to finish strongly if the race is truly run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse And Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya sets a fierce freak gallop that burns out the field, leaving a late outsider to scavenge.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Daboya's single-front-runner status and the absence of a rival to force the pace; Berto Ramirez or Rakki, operating from further back than ideal, would be the unlikely beneficiaries if the front genuinely collapses.

watchPoints.text: Watch Daboya's early splits — if Sam Coen (5lb claimer) allows a very slow crawl, the race becomes a sprint finish and the hold-up horses drawn into midfield may not be able to generate enough momentum.
Expound's 93-day layoff is the biggest unknown in the race; if he arrives short of peak fitness, the second prominent slot disappears and Daboya becomes even more unopposed at the front.

Churchwarden, Rakki, and Berto Ramirez are all genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield — if all three drop back to their natural position at the rear as the race unfolds, it creates a significant gap in the middle of the field and could leave Daboya with no cover to judge pace against.

Merlin The Wizard with 7lb apprentice Reese Holohan is worth monitoring in the market — any significant support would suggest connections believe the horse can adapt its hold-up style to sit closer in this slow-pace scenario.

races.name: Brennan's Pharmacy Handicap

runners_data.name: Delta
runners_data.note: J J Slevin's booking is the key upgrade here — the four-year-old has a win at 12f on Good ground and is a genuine front-runner whose last run (37 days ago) was a modest effort at 15f, but the drop back to 16f over Good turf suits; needs to avoid a three-way pace war with Dream On Baby and Miss Gitana.

runners_data.name: Filey Bay
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with strong course-and-distance profile (won at 17f on Good) and Simon Torrens in the plate; Emmet Mullins's 2/16 recent strike rate is modest but the horse's 3W4P record at similar going gives him genuine claims from a prominent position if the front-runners tire.

runners_data.name: Clear Quartz
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose best recent effort was a second at 9f on Soft, raising a slight question over this two-mile trip; the 7lb claim from Harnett helps, and if the front three set a strong pace this horse's closing style becomes very relevant — the 19-day turnaround is fine.

runners_data.name: Plontier
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with two Good-ground placed efforts in his history, though OR=83 and a modest 0W1P at similar going flags limited upside; Reese Holohan takes 7lb off and the two-mile trip suits a patient horse if he can find cover — recent form string (/60-20) shows some positives.

runners_data.name: Spasiba
runners_data.note: The 587-day absence is the dominant concern here — last ran in a point-to-point and returns for W P Mullins with Ben Coen aboard, which is an obvious plus; won at 16f on Good ground and showed real class when younger, but the layoff makes this a speculative angle however obvious the trainer-jockey combination looks.

runners_data.name: Dream On Baby
runners_data.note: Running just two days after his last start is a significant red flag for a six-year-old tackling two miles on Good ground; Emmet Mullins knows the horse well and he has winning form at 16f, but a front-running style in a three-way pace battle off a 48-hour turnaround raises serious stamina doubts late on.

runners_data.name: Zoffman
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on a losing run (70-680) whose best Going-going effort was a win at OR level around two years ago; Gary Carroll is a competent navigator but the 64-day break and declining form make this one to watch rather than trust — the headgear note (hg:p) suggests connections are searching for an answer.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: Placed three times from hold-up but genuinely pressed wide by the depth of this field's closer contingent — in practice this horse is unlikely to get its preferred rearmost position and will race closer than ideal; the 0W1P record at similar going and modest OR=74 make it hard to see how racing out of role improves matters, though the 5lb claim from Nicola Burns helps marginally.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who fades in finishes — the ⚠ tag says everything here; over two miles with Delta and Dream On Baby also pressing for the lead, Miss Gitana is likely to be outgunned for position early and then emptied in the straight, making the OR=63 figure look generous rather than attractive.

races.paceDynamic: Delta, Dream On Baby, and Miss Gitana are all confirmed front-runners in a nine-runner field over two miles on Good ground at Tramore, making a strong early gallop virtually certain as all three will attempt to press for position from the outset. The resulting pace is likely to be genuinely searching over this stamina-testing trip, with the leaders pressing each other through the early and middle stages, burning through reserves that will matter in the final quarter-mile. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and midfield horses with proven stamina — those who can sit off the contested pace, conserve energy, and reel in tying leaders late — over horses who will be embroiled in the pace battle itself. The field holds more front-running types than can all dominate comfortably; of the three, Delta (with the benefit of J J Slevin and the best recent form) is most likely to secure the lead, with Dream On Baby pressing hard from an awkward two-day turnaround and Miss Gitana likely to be crowded out and lose her natural position early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Delta and Dream On Baby press each other hard from the start and burn the front-runners out over the two-mile trip
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop will see leaders tire inside the final two furlongs, leaving the race open for hold-up or midfield horses to come through on the bridle; genuine stayers with cover through the middle stages are perfectly placed to capitalise

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Delta Controls And Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Delta is allowed to dictate a measured gallop from the front and J J Slevin manages the pace intelligently
scenarios.body: With Slevin able to control tempo rather than burn Delta out in a three-way fight, the four-year-old's Good-ground form (1W4P at similar going) becomes a major asset over this stamina trip; a well-judged lead at a sustainable clip could leave pursuers with too much to do

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but uneven, with mid-division horses tracking into a position to challenge smoothly from two furlongs out
scenarios.body: Spasiba's one-time Listed-winning class and Ben Coen's tactical awareness could see the W P Mullins runner (returning after 587 days) slot into a perfect tracking position and deliver late; Filey Bay's course experience at this distance also fits a race where midfield becomes the sweet spot

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the front three falter simultaneously and the race fragments into a ragged finish with no horse travelling well
scenarios.body: A chaotic pace scenario with multiple leaders strung out could produce a muddling finish where the best-weighted or freshest legs prevail regardless of style; however this shape is the least likely given Good ground and experienced handlers at the front

watchPoints.text: Delta, Dream On Baby, and Miss Gitana all attempting to lead over two miles — watch the first two furlongs to see who blinks first, as the loser of that three-way battle for the front could drop out catastrophically from the middle stages onward.

Dream On Baby ran just 48 hours ago — watch for signs of flatness or reluctance in the parade ring and early in the race; if Robbie Colgan has to push to hold his position early, the horse may not last the two miles.

Spasiba returns after 587 days for W P Mullins and Ben Coen — watch the market closely for any support, as any significant money for a stable that rarely runs horses cold would be a material intelligence signal worth noting.

Clear Quartz has predominantly run at shorter trips (best effort at 9f) and is stepping sharply up to 16f — watch whether Joseph Harnett gives the horse a conservative ride to conserve stamina or tries to position prominently, which could tell you whether the team trusts the trip.

Miss Gitana is tagged as fading in finishes and faces two stronger front-runners — if she is pushed wide or immediately outpaced at the start, she can be safely discounted from the race outcome very early.

races.name: Dan Cowman Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a recent second over 2m on Good going (9 days ago) giving strong course confidence; Denis Hogan's runner wears a hood and tongue-tie, and the 9-day turnaround is fresh enough, but needs the pace to truly collapse in the straight to reel back leaders from the rear.

runners_data.name: Vervain
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type with two placings in last five runs, ridden by a 7lb claimer who adds value on the weight; recent Good-ground form encouraging with a second and fourth on that surface, and the 12f-12f form may be stretching slightly over 2m but this trip is not prohibitive.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer placed in five of fifteen runs on similar going; the 5lb claim from Sam Coen helps trim the weight burden, and a recent second over 14f suggests the step up to 2m should suit — however, this horse needs a strong pace to make the ground from behind, which may not materialise here.

runners_data.name: Bynx
runners_data.note: The best handicap form in the field with three wins and eight places from thirteen similar-going runs; naturally a deep hold-up horse who has won over course-equivalent trips, but with several other closers compressed toward the rear, Ben Coen will find it harder than usual to find clear space — true potential partially muted by race shape.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose best efforts come over 2m+ on Good ground, but the surplus of back-markers in this race means Sadhbh Tormey may find this runner forced to race less patiently than ideal; three places from five runs at this trip on Good is solid form, though a win has proven elusive.

runners_data.name: Bhean Saibhre
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose second over 2m on Good going is directly relevant and who is well-positioned in the race shape to track Gallo Dell Cielo from early on; Nicola Burns claims 5lb, the 25-day freshener looks acceptable, and Good turf suits based on repeated positives in that going — a key player in the likely scenario.

runners_data.name: Gallo Dell Cielo
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner, and while the STYLE_FIT tag reflects it racing in a role that may not be its absolute optimum, it has won twice on Standard (comparable) ground and sets the pace for the whole field; 185 days off the track is a significant concern, and its Good-ground form is limited to just six runs with one placing — watch closely for signs of ring rust.

runners_data.name: Kings Gesture
runners_data.note: Out-of-form hold-up horse flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, with zero wins or places in seven Good-going runs — the worst finishing profile in the field; Reese Holohan claims 7lb but the trainer has no recent runners in the 14-day window, and being pushed closer to midfield than it naturally runs is an additional negative.

runners_data.name: Fire Coral
runners_data.note: Veteran 7-year-old with solid form at long distances (22f-24f) on Good ground — two wins and four places from fifteen similar-going starts — but the drop to 2m might not play to its strengths; a genuine closer who has earned its redistribution into midfield, and Scott McCullagh will be hopeful of a clean run late.

runners_data.name: Highway Sixty One
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old who races prominently and has finished second over 12f on Good, but stepping up to 2m for the first time and the longer trip is an unknown; Gary Carroll's booking is notable for a horse with upside, and a midfield-to-prominent position in this race should be within reach — trip is the question mark.

runners_data.name: Synchronize
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a second over 13f and fourth over 16f on Good ground, making 2m a plausible stretch; Julian Pietropaolo's 7lb claim helps, but 39 days since the last run and a compressed field will make it difficult to find the late run that suits this horse's profile.

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent/hold-up type with a second over 16f on Good ground in recent history; Robbie Colgan's experience is an asset in a tricky field, and despite the age, a prior placing over 2m suggests the stamina is genuine — but consistency has been an issue and winning form is absent in the last five.

runners_data.name: Stone Rulya
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner on OR=60 but flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, with zero wins or places across seven Good-going starts and an incomplete record — no jockey declared which is a notable negative; the headgear combination (tongue-strap/eye shield/visor) suggests the trainer is experimenting, and the form line of 008-47 offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: Out-of-form closer with a worrying recent record (409-00) and flagged for fading late — the least likely beneficiary of this race shape; no jockey declared is a concern, and being a genuine back-marker squeezed into midfield in a slow-pace race removes whatever chance this horse might have in a truly searching gallop.

races.paceDynamic: Gallo Dell Cielo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 2m handicap on Good turf at Tramore, and with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, this horse should be able to dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front without significant pressure. The pace is therefore likely to be sustainable rather than searching, which typically compresses the field and reduces the advantage for true hold-up horses who rely on a strong end-to-end gallop to reel back rivals. Bhean Saibhre and Highway Sixty One are the most natural prominent racers likely to slot in just behind Gallo Dell Cielo and take the spots immediately off the leader, giving them the ideal stalking position if the leader fades late. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or in the first third of the field and quicken from there, as the measured pace is unlikely to set up a meaningful late surge for genuine back-markers. The field contains substantially more hold-up horses than there are rear positions available — Bynx, Maxwell Smart, Kings Gesture, Fire Coral, Synchronize, and Crypto Crash are all true hold-up types who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they naturally prefer, making their effective style in this race closer to midfield, and most are unlikely to secure their natural position at the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gallo Dell Cielo Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Gallo Dell Cielo leads without being pressed and sets a controlled pace that suits a prominent finisher.
scenarios.body: Gallo Dell Cielo rolls along in front at a comfortable tempo, burning off rivals gradually through the final half-mile, with the prominent stalkers Bhean Saibhre and Highway Sixty One best positioned to mow down any weakness; horses racing genuinely off the pace will find the steady gallop does not generate enough late suction.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Gallo Dell Cielo fades turning for home and the horses tracking in second and third sweep past in the straight.
scenarios.body: Bhean Saibhre or Highway Sixty One, having conserved energy in a close-stalking role, hit the front with enough in reserve to hold on, while a horse like Vervain or God Of Thunder — who has the form at this trip on Good going — finishes strongly from just behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally stronger than expected and genuine closers benefit from a fast-finishing burst in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse racing in a true hold-up role would need to close from well back, but given the redistribution of multiple closer-types into midfield, the field is likely bunched, reducing the runway; only a horse with genuinely superior class or a peak run, such as Bynx — who won over C&D-equivalent trip on Good — could manage it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Interference
scenarios.trigger: If the field becomes compressed mid-race and traffic problems shuffle positions dramatically in the straight.
scenarios.body: With 14 runners on a turning track, interference in the home straight is plausible and could advantage a horse that finds a clean passage late or has a patient jockey; this scenario randomly benefits any horse with late pace held in reserve, but is more a lottery than a structural advantage.

watchPoints.text: Gallo Dell Cielo's fitness after 185 days off is the single biggest swing factor — if it weakens sharply turning for home, the entire race shape changes and prominent types like Bhean Saibhre and Highway Sixty One are the direct beneficiaries.

With 14 runners on Tramore's tight turning course, watch for traffic problems in the home straight — any horse with a patient jockey and a clear run in the final two furlongs, particularly Bynx with Ben Coen in the saddle, could emerge from a bunched field late.

Stone Rulya and Crypto Crash both have no jockey declared and are flagged for fading in the finish — if either drifts across other runners or causes interference in the straight, it could compromise the chances of genuine contenders racing near them.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Bynx, Maxwell Smart, Kings Gesture, Fire Coral, Synchronize, Crypto Crash) all racing closer to midfield than usual means the middle of the field will be congested — watch for pace quickening suddenly at the top of the straight catching several of these horses flat-footed.

Highway Sixty One's trip stamina over 2m is untested — Gary Carroll will need to manage this horse's energy carefully in the early stages given the lack of pace pressure, and if it gets too close too soon it could empty rapidly in the final furlong.
